1.0 
INTRODUCTION 
1.1 
Scope 
This plan applies to all Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment (SAME) hardware, software, and 
operating procedures developed under the Microgravity Research, Development, and Operations Contract 
(MRDOC).  This plan establishes the methods and responsibilities for verifying the SAME requirements. 
 The requirements for the SAME project, including investigation, engineering, product assurance, safety, 
and carrier requirements, are in Appendix A of this document.  The verification methods and sources of 
these requirements are also included in Appendix A.  This plan defines the verification process, leading to 
certification of the SAME flight hardware. 
1.2 
Purpose 
This document defines the verification activities required to show that SAME complies with its 
requirements.  These activities include the verification of investigation requirements from the Exploration 
Investigation Requirements Document (EIRD) for SAME, software engineering requirements from the 
Software Requirements Documents, product assurance requirements from the Project Product Assurance 
Plan (PAP), safety requirements from the Hazard Reports, and carrier requirements from the Microgravity 
Science Glovebox (MSG) Interface Control Document (ICD). 
This document includes all of the requirements to be verified by SAME and serves as the Engineering 
Requirements Document to organize and list all necessary requirements. 
1.3 
TBDs 
TBDs are used as a place-holder for requirements, verifications, or document numbers that are not known 
at the time of the latest release of this document.

4.0 
VERIFICATIONS 
4.1 
General 
The SAME Project Office will verify all the requirements imposed on the SAME System.  The primary 
sites for verification activities will be the Glenn Research Center (GRC) and the item developer’s site 
unless otherwise directed by the MSG or International Space Station (ISS) programs.  All requirements 
will be recorded in this document and disseminated to the design team.  This document will provide 
traceability from the parent requirement through the subsequent derived requirements.  It will also 
identify the verification source document and verification method.  
SAME will be building and verifying more than one set of flight hardware. Consequently, a certain 
number of verifications must be repeated for each serialized assembly. A subset of the requirements is 
designated as series requirements.  
4.1.1 Verification Methods 
The methods used to complete the verifications are analysis, test, inspection and demonstration.  The 
method(s) required for the SAME verifications are listed in the requirements matrix in Appendix A.  The 
methods of verification are defined in MSFC-RQMT-2888 as stated in Sections 4.1.1.1, 4.1.1.2, 4.1.1.3, 
and 4.1.1.4. 
4.1.1.1 Analysis 
Analysis is a technical evaluation that relates equipment design and use parameters for prediction of 
actual design and operation.  Analysis may be used to verify requirements, provided established 
techniques used are adequate to yield confidence, or where testing is impractical.  Included in this 
category is analysis of similarity to items previously verified to the same criteria or more stringent 
criteria.  Verification accomplished by analysis shall be evidenced by an analysis report. 
4.1.1.2 Test 
Test is actual operation of equipment under simulated conditions or the subjection of equipment to 
specified environments to measure responses.  Verification accomplished by test shall be evidenced by a 
test report. 
4.1.1.3 Inspection 
Inspection is a physical evaluation of equipment and associated documentation.  Inspection may be used 
to verify construction features, drawing compliance, workmanship, and physical condition.  It includes 
determination of physical dimensions.  Verification accomplished by inspection shall be evidenced by an 
inspection report. 
4.1.1.4 Demonstration 
Demonstration is the qualitative determination of compliance with requirements by observation during 
actual operation or simulation under preplanned conditions and guidelines.  Some human factor 
requirements where the method of closure is a demonstration require the investigation to be set up in its 
on-orbit configuration in the MSG Engineering Unit (EU) to verify that the requirement is satisfied.

SAME-PLN-005 Rev F 
 4
4.1.2 Tools (Requirements Matrix and Verification Tracking Log) 
A matrix has been compiled in an Excel spreadsheet to include all requirements to be satisfied by SAME. 
 It identifies the source of each requirement, the discipline under which it falls, the verification method to 
be used for closure, and resources necessary to perform the verification. It also identifies series 
requirements. The matrix, in Appendix A, will be provided to the engineering team for use in verification 
activities, and will be included in the released (.pdf) version of this document. 
The verification tracking log (VTL) will be used to track the status of the verifications and the 
documentation provided as evidence for the completion of the verifications. It is an Excel workbook that 
includes five worksheets: the VTL itself, a statistics page, the current version of the requirements matrix, 
a summary of applicable ECOs, and a notes/explanation page. The VTL will not be configuration-
controlled as it is a summary of the state of controlled documentation and it will not be included in the 
released version of this document. It will be available in the project team’s shared directory. 
4.2 
Planning 
4.2.1 Verification Definition Sheets 
A Verification Definition Sheet (VDS) will be used to complete the carrier requirements from MSFC-
ICD-3462.  The corresponding VDS for each carrier requirement is listed in the requirements matrix and 
can be found in Appendix E of MSFC-RQMT-2888.  The VDS provides instructions, definitions, 
references, and guidelines for verification activities associated with each requirement. 
4.2.2 Test Plans and Procedures 
The controlled requirements matrix will be distributed to the engineering team so that the requirements 
can be grouped into meaningful test plans or procedures that will allow for efficient testing and closure of 
the requirements.  Test plans and procedures will be written to include the verification statements to 
ensure that the requirements are clearly stated, understood, and closed out by the test.  Test plans and 
procedures containing carrier requirements will also contain the corresponding VDS. 
Test plans and procedures will be a project team effort lead by the Systems Engineering team.  Plans and 
procedures will use exact language from the requirement sources to convey the objective of the test as 
completion of these verifications.   
The template of how the requirements will be incorporated into the documents is shown in Figure 1.  This 
table, along with the introductory text, will be included in test plans and procedures intended for 
verification activities. 
4.2.3 Implementation and Reporting 
4.2.3.1 Implementation 
Test verifications in the matrix will be logically grouped into similar items that can be completed in a 
single test.  The test plans and procedures will be written accordingly.  Some of the verifications will be 
closed on the functional model or other similar flight-like hardware when the testing of flight hardware is 
not necessary or cannot be accomplished due to the nature of the test.  Otherwise, testing will be done on 
the flight hardware.  The tests performed on non-flight hardware are indicated in the requirements matrix.

SAME-PLN-005 Rev F 
 5
Inspections will be done at the time of hardware assembly and will be done on flight hardware or flight 
drawings.   
Analyses will be done using the flight configuration of hardware for the calculations.   
Demonstrations will be done on the flight hardware.   
All Human Factors (HFIT) verifications will be done once the hardware is delivered to MSG and the 
HFIT evaluation is performed.  Additional verifications require integrated setup or testing in the MSG EU 
and will be completed after the hardware is delivered to MSG.  These verifications are identified in the 
requirements matrix. 
 
Figure 1: Example of Verification List in Documents 
4.2.3.2 Reporting 
Test, analysis and inspection reports will be written as evidence that the tests, analyses and inspections 
were performed to satisfy the requirements.  Reports will include the requirement statements, as shown in 
Figure 1, to indicate what verifications were performed and are closed by the report.  Reports and other 
necessary documentation will be kept by the Systems Engineering team and Configuration Management 
as evidence that the verifications were performed.  
The final report generated against a carrier requirement will be a comprehensive report intended to close 
out the requirement, upon which a Certificate of Compliance is issued. 
Certificates of Compliance will be generated to close verifications by demonstration.

SAME-PLN-005 Rev F 
 6
4.3 
Certificate of Compliance  
As the carrier verification activities are completed, the SAME team will generate and sign Certificates of 
Compliance.  With the completion of all verifications identified in this document and their associated 
Certificates of Compliance, all of the requirements and verifications of MSG compatibility, functionality, 
and safety will have been met. 
4.4 
Maintenance of the Certificate of Compliance 
Any changes to SAME occurring after the verification activities are completed will be reviewed to assess 
their impacts on the individual requirements and their associated verification certificates.   If such a 
review determines that re-verification is warranted, the changes to SAME and the proposed additional 
verification activities will be presented to the MSG payload program office for concurrence before 
verification activities are completed.  
4.5 
Requirement Sources  
4.5.1 Investigation Requirements 
The investigation requirements for SAME are found in the EIRD for SAME.  These, along with derived 
engineering responses to these requirements from the various engineering disciplines, can be found in the 
requirements matrix in this document.  These engineering responses will be verified to show that the 
investigation requirements are met.  The Project Scientist for SAME will approve all reports containing 
investigation verification close-outs.    
4.5.2 Software Engineering Requirements 
Software engineering requirements can be found in SAME-DOC-004, Software Requirements Document, 
and are included in the requirements matrix in this document.  These requirements include detailed 
responses to the investigation, safety, and MSG carrier requirements, and requirements to establish good 
engineering practices. 
4.5.3 Product Assurance Requirements 
Product assurance requirements can be found in SAME-PLN-003, Product Assurance Plan.  The 
requirements found in the Product Assurance Plan are derived from the Space Assurance Requirements 
and Guidelines (SARG) as they are applicable to the SAME project.  Statements containing “shall” 
require a formal documented closure of the requirement, as defined in the Product Assurance Plan, and 
are included in the requirements matrix.  Statements containing “will or must” are requirements to be 
fulfilled but do not require a formal documented closure, as defined in the Product Assurance Plan.  The 
“will or must” requirements which have a direct impact on the SAME project budget, schedule, and 
design are included in the requirements matrix. 
4.5.4 Safety Requirements 
SAME safety requirements are identified according to the payload safety process described in NSTS 
1700.7B, Safety Policy and Requirements for Payloads Using the Space Transportation System, and 
NSTS 1700.7B ISS Addendum, Safety Policy and Requirements for Payloads Using the International 
Space Station, using NSTS/ISS 13830, Payload Safety Review and Data Submittal.

SAME-PLN-005 Rev F 
 7
The SAME safety requirements are found in the SAME hazard reports and are included in the 
requirements matrix in this document.  The requirements are included in the matrix to provide visibility 
and to allow them to be grouped with other requirements in verification activities (i.e. test plans and 
procedures) for efficient completion. Although closure information will be included in the VTL, the 
safety requirements will be officially tracked in a Safety Verification Tracking Log (SVTL) and 
maintained by the SAME Safety Engineer.  The SVTL and documentation used to close the safety 
verifications will be provided to the Payload Safety Review Panel (PSRP) for approval at the Phase III 
Safety Review. 
4.5.5 MSG Carrier Requirements 
Requirements for interfacing with the MSG are found in MSFC-ICD-3462, Microgravity Science 
Glovebox (MSG) Interface Control Document for SAME, and are included in the requirements matrix in 
this document.  MSFC-ICD-3462 contains a Verification Applicability Matrix to indicate what 
requirements from MSFC-RQMT-2888 are applicable to SAME.  The Verification Applicability Matrix 
also identifies the appropriate verification method, the applicable VDS, and other comments associated 
with the completion of the verification.  All information given in the Verification Applicability Matrix is 
duplicated in the requirements matrix in this document.  The complete text of the requirements as well as 
the VDS is found in MSFC-RQMT-2888. 
4.5.6 Space Shuttle and ISS Requirements 
MSG interfaces with Johnson Space Center (JSC) concerning payload interface requirements.  Therefore, 
all Space Shuttle and ISS requirements should be documented in MSFC-ICD-3462, as identified in 
Section 4.5.4. 
4.5.7 KSC Facility Requirements 
SAME is not planning to operate at Kennedy Space Center (KSC). 
4.6 
Staffing 
Implementation of the SAME verification process requires all members of the SAME team to support the 
verification activities. 
4.6.1 Roles and Responsibilities 
The Systems Engineering team will prepare documentation necessary for the performance of verifications 
and the reporting of the results of verification activities.  All plans and procedures for verification 
activities will be checked by a member of the Systems Engineering team to insure that the applicable 
requirements are included.   One member of the Systems Engineering team will be responsible for 
updating the VTL to track the status of the verification activities and to include the document number for 
the reports generated to close the verifications.   
Hardware and Software Engineers will provide assistance writing test plans and procedures and 
performing verification activities. 
The Safety Engineer will track and maintain all safety verifications from the hazard reports in the SVTL. 
The Project Scientist will approve all documentation that completes an investigation requirement. 
Quality Assurance (QA) personnel will be involved if the requirement in question is a QA requirement.

5.0

When viewing the original electronic files of this document, the requirements matrix can be found in an 
Excel spreadsheet with the same name as this document.  The hardcopy of this document and the .pdf 
version will include the requirements matrix at time of release in Appendix A. 
In addition to requirements to be verified, the matrix contains section titles and parent requirements that 
provide additional information to aid in the understanding of the verification activities.  The items that are 
not verifiable requirements are designated in the matrix as indicated in Table 1.

Load Requirements
Investigations will be designed to withstand the launch and 
landing conditions when stowed in the MPLM, Middeck or other 
transportation vehicles. For design consideration the 
Investigation will use the acceleration loads defined in Table I 
when stowed in the MPLM or Middeck. These loads are based 
on a worst case condition of the Middeck and MPLM. The IIT will 
provide the investigator with the acceleration and random 
vibration data of the carrier the investigation is manifested on. 
Additional requirements or data may be required depending on 
the configuration of the investigation and the requirements of the 
carrier.
It is assumed that the loads imposed by the random vibration 
environment on stowed items in foam can be neglected in design 
consideration. The Investigation will conduct a workmanship test, 
for instance on electrical components or mechanisms, based on 
the random vibration environment defined in Table I. The 
Investigation must ensure that the hardware will survive the 
workmanship random vibration level.

Reverse Current
Investigation hardware connected to the 120 Vdc primary power 
source available in the WV must comply with the requirements 
defined in paragraph 3.2.2.4.1 or 3.2.2.4.2 for the reverse current 
into the upstream power source. Note: Investigations having

less than 25 micro-farads, are considered meeting the limits of 
paragraph 3.2.2.4.1 for US Type I RPCMs. Input connected 
capacitors are those which, by virtue of circuit arrangement, are 
able to discharge through the power source when the power 
source is short circuited. Series connected rectifier diodes and 
resistors greater than 10 Ohms are sufficient to block such 
discharges.

Reverse Current Limits
Investigations using the 120V DC primary power source shall 
limit reverse current transients that can occur when a hard fault 
occurs across the power source within the applicable transient 
envelope shown in Figures 15, 16 and 17. For purposes of this 
interface definition, the fault is 10 milli Ohms or less applied 
within 2 micro-seconds or less. For the investigation hardware 
exhibiting reverse current transient peaks within ±100 Amperes, 
the fault resistance is 40 milli Ohms or less.

322.4.2
MSFC-RQMT-2888 
3.2.2.4.2
Electrical 
Engineering
Transients Partially Contained Within the Envelope
If the reverse current on the 120V DC primary power source 
exceeds the envelope limits defined in paragraph 3.2.2.4.1 for 
one or more short time intervals, the transient peak current and 
the ratio of the times of intersection with the envelope shall 
satisfy the following inequality: (ipk/ie)2 x ln(t2/t1) ≤ 1 where ln 
represents the natural logarithm, t1 and t2 correspond to the 
beginning and end times, respectively, of each interval when the 
transient is outside the envelope, ipk is the peak of the transient 
occurring between t2 and t1, and ie is the point on the envelope at 
the time of the peak ipk. For multiple intervals in which the 
envelope is exceeded, the left-hand side of this expression will 
be evaluated for each interval and the sum of all such results will 
total less than unity.  See MSFC-RQMT-2888 for more 
information.

Electrical Bonding 
Investigation hardware connected to the RPDA power sources 
available in the WV shall be bonded in accordance with the 
following requirements. Electrical bonding is the process of 
providing good electrical connection across mechanical 
interfaces to minimize electrical potential differences between 
equipment and individual parts of structure. Good electrical 
bonding provides: Fault current paths for protection against fire 
and personnel shock, Provides a current path for radio 
frequencies for proper operation of filters and shields, and a 
means to prevent or safely discharge static charges.
Electrical bonds are classified according to the purpose for the 
bond. There may be more than one purpose for bonding a 
specific interface, and the bond shall meet the requirements of 
each applicable class. Notes shall be provided on assembly 
drawings indicating the applicable class or classes. The material 
used in the MSG work volume is 7075 aluminum nickel struck. A 
bonding test shall be performed during integrated testing with the 
Engineering Unit.

Fault current, due to short circuits to equipment case or 
structure, may cause shock or fire hazards. All electrically 
conductive equipment cases that may develop potentials due to 
short circuits shall be electrically bonded to structure. The bond 
shall minimize shock hazard voltages and allow proper operation 
of circuit protection devices such as circuit breakers or fuses. 
Bonding of structural joints in the fault current return path shall 
provide for the maximum current that may be delivered by the 
power supply until the fuse or circuit breaker disconnects. For 
personnel and fire safety the fault current return path shall be 
capable of conducting a minimum of 500% overload current for a 
time period of 0.5 second. Typical personnel protection breakers 
will trip within 0.2 second after a hard short to case. Resultant 
voltage on the enclosure of the affected component must not 
exceed 4.5 volts, and no fire or damage to the bond is allowed.

Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) equal to or less than 4,000 V to 
the case or any pin on external connectors. EPCE that may be 
damaged by ESD between 4,000 and 15,000 V shall have a label 
affixed to the case in a location clearly visible in the installed 
position. Handling of EPCE susceptible to ESD up to 15,000 V 
shall be in accordance with MIL-STD-1686. These voltages are 
the result of charges that may be accumulated and discharged 
from ground personnel or crewmembers during equipment 
installation or removal.
Analysis and Inspection will be used to close 
this requirement.

digital outputs, split equally between two connectors in the Work

Low Rate Data Link (LRDL) in a Low Rate Telemetry (LRT) 
packet. The digital output lines are controlled via commands to 
the RC.

be used to determine if the AHU heat exchanger is capable of 
removing the dissipated heat load. The filtration system provides 
for particulate removal, filtration of single spillage (see section 
3.7.3), and oxidation of CO to CO2 by means of a built-in 
catalyst. Due to the hydroscopic nature of the filters, the humidity

Chemical Releases
Investigations that use chemicals that would create a toxicity 
problem or cause a hazard to ISS or MSG hardware if released 
shall provide adequate containment.  Containment shall be 
provided by the use of a pressure vessel or the use of two or 
three redundantly sealed containers, depending on the 
toxicological hazard for a chemical with a vapor pressure below 
15 psia. The Investigation must assure that each level of 
containment will not leak under the maximum use conditions (i.e. 
vibration, temperature, pressure, etc.). The release of methanol, 
ethanol, isopropyl alcohol, n-propyl alcohol, n-butyl alcohol, 
acetone, ethylene glycol, and propylene glycol into the ISS 
habitable environment shall be prohibited. The release of these 
compounds due to normal materials offgassing is exempt from 
this requirement.

Procedural Hazard Controls
Investigations shall be responsible for using crew procedures to 
control the MSG hazards specified below. Depending on the 
investigation, some of these hazards may not be applicable.
a. Investigation crew procedures shall have a step(s) that directs 
the crew to purge the MSG work volume for 2 minutes following 
the use of the Nitrogen system. If the MSG is in normal mode, 
then the work volume can be purged by opening a sideport or 
gloveport. (Reference Payload Hazard Report (PHR) MSG-FL4, 
control 1)

Barcoding
Investigators will coordinate with the MSG IIT and the IIT will 
coordinate with NASA/JSC organization OC for Inventory 
Management System (IMS) barcodes. All equipment shall have 
an IMS barcode in accordance with SSP 50007. IMS barcode 
placeholders shall be present on engineering drawings, if the 
standard hardware ID label (with IMS barcode included) is not 
used. If the IMS barcode is ordered from the DDPF, the Decal 
Catalog decal part number should be included in a note on the 
engineering drawing.
